Creating Health Informatics Dashboard

Author

Yu Cheng Hsu

Getting WHO Observatory Data Source

WHO Observatory

The Global Health Observatory (GHO) is the World Health Organization’s (WHO) dedicated platform designed to enable users to explore a vast array of health data from around the world. Its primary purpose is to provide accessible, comprehensive insights into health-related indicators and country-specific data, supporting informed decision-making in global public health.

Key features include an extensive collection of health indicators, and detailed country profiles. The platform covers many general health indicators including mortality and burden of diseases, the Millennium Development Goals (child nutrition, child health, maternal and reproductive health, immunization, HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, neglected diseases, water and sanitation), non-communicable diseases and risk factors, epidemic-prone diseases, health systems, environmental health, violence and injuries, equity among others.

Introducing Power BI

Power BI is one of the most popular business visualization tools for designing dashboards for business intelligence and data analytics. Some other options you might have seen before include Tableau, Qlik Sense, or ArcGIS. The following workshop will demonstrate how to build a dashboard from scratch.

Import Data

First things first, we need data to visualize. Power BI supports data retrieval from three categories:

  1. Direct import
  2. Import from database
  3. Import from API

Import from API

In this example, 1. select OData 2. and input https://ghoapi.azureedge.net/api. Currently, we need to find the documentation of the GHO data, so

  1. select DIMENSION, IndicatorDimension, Indicator, and RegionCountry.

You can have a glimpse of the imported data at the Table view tab, and it works similarly to Excel.

Link Up Data

All the tables in GHO are designed and stored in spatial dimensions, and the actual name of the country is stored separately. We need to indicate such facts to let the program know what these codes stand for.

Visualizing the Data

After aggregating all the data, we can design our dashboard. The process of building up the tool is:

  1. Select visualization tool
  2. Select data needed to display in the visualization tool
  3. Configure the tool

Landing Page: Newly Infected HIV Cases Worldwide

On the first page, we would like to inform the user about the newly infected HIV cases in the world.

Exercise

Name the data source and column you need.

  1. In the Visualizations pane (right side), click the Filled map icon.
  2. From the Fields pane, drag your location field (i.e., CountryName) to the Location bucket in the Visualizations pane.
  3. Switch to the “Format visual” tab (paintbrush icon).
  4. Under Fill colors > Colors, click the fx icon next to Default color to open the conditional formatting dialog.
  5. Set Format style to Gradient.
  6. Choose New HIV Cases (i.e., NumericValue in the newly infected HIV table). Summarize it using SUM and drop NA values.
  7. Define colors: i.e., Light blue for Minimum (low cases), Dark red for Maximum (high cases). Add a middle color (i.e., yellow) for a three-color gradient.
  8. Rename the visual title by clicking the arrow next to Location -> Rename for this visual.

Adding Tooltips for Clarity and Interactivity

  1. Add the same information to the tooltip box to let the exact information display on the tooltips.
  2. Rename the visual title by clicking the arrow next to Tooltips -> Rename for this visual.

Adding Filter

There are two ways of adding a filter:

  • Filter pane
  • Slicer

We will add a slicer to let the user select a specific time range in the map:

  1. Select the Slicer visual from the Visualizations pane.
  2. In the Fields pane, locate your data table.
  3. Drag the TimeDim column to the “Field” bucket in the Visualizations pane.
  4. Adjust the slicer settings in the format visual pane.

For the filter pane, it works in a similar manner except you just need to drop them in the filter pane and choose the scope of filtering.

Create the scatter plot Chart (TB Incidence vs. New HIV by TimeDim)

  1. Add a Scatter chart visual
  2. Drag NumericValue from TB_Incidence_HIV_Pos_per_100K” to X-axis.
  3. Drag NumericValue from New_HIV_Infections to Y-axis.
  4. Drag TimeDim to Values

Format:

  • Title: “TB Incidence rate among HIV positive per 100K people and TB Incidence rate per 100K people by TimeDim”.
  • X-axis: Label “TB Incidence rate among HIV positive per 100K people”
  • Y-axis: Label “TB Incidence rate per 100K people”

Analytics: 1. Go to further analysis tab 2. Turn on trend line
